verdict.rationale: Zep documents per-user Context Graphs, which keep a user's memory separate. It also mentions shared Context Graphs (account, project, or business-domain graphs) and ABAC policies on API keys and UserGroups that limit which context each agent or Memory MCP user can reach, which together imply selective sharing with private boundaries. However, the evidence never shows an explicit group-memory workflow: how a shared graph is created, how agents or users are assigned to it, or how specific memories are selected for sharing while others stay private. Missing for 10: explicit shared/group graph creation and membership docs, a mechanism for choosing which memory is shared versus private, policy examples scoping shared versus private graphs, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can share selected memory across multiple agents or users (team or group memory) while keeping private memory private
